title: Reachable Nodes With Restrictions
summary: Given an undirected tree with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1 and edges defined by a 2D array, and a list of restricted nodes, determine the largest number of nodes reachable from node 0 without visiting any restricted node.
statement: Given an undirected tree with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1 and edges defined by a 2D array, and a list of restricted nodes, determine the largest number of nodes reachable from node 0 without visiting any restricted node.
constraints: The n nodes and n-1 undirected edges form a tree rooted for this task at node 0.
A traversal may not enter any node listed in restricted; node 0 is never restricted.
Return how many nodes remain reachable from node 0.
hints: Build adjacency lists for the undirected tree.
Initialize the visited set with every restricted node so traversal can never enter one.
Traverse from node 0, marking each newly discovered neighbor and counting popped nodes.
A tree node is reachable exactly when the traversal can follow its unique path from 0 without encountering a blocked node.
editorial: A tree node is reachable exactly when the traversal can follow its unique path from 0 without encountering a blocked node.

tests.explanation: Blocking nodes 4 and 5 also cuts off node 6; nodes 0,1,2,3 remain reachable, giving four.
Restricted node 1 blocks both itself and the path to node 2, leaving only node 0.
